clue.text: A court's opening lines

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. railway lines

explanation.surface: A court's first words of proceedings, its opening lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening lines' reads as the start of a speech, but splits into a chance (opening) and railway lines (RY). The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court.

clue.text: Exceptional care's needed about parking for dances

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the parking symbol
exceptional suggests the letters are taken out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S counting as a letter here
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Unusual attention is required near the car park for a dance event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges CARES into CAERS, and 'about' puts P inside: CA-P-ERS. 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers are playful leaps, frisky dances.

clue.text: Expert — as French drivers go

definitions.meaning: in French, to the right, the side of the road traffic keeps to in France

explanation.surface: A skilled motorist, by French standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful, and read as French it says 'to the right', where traffic in France keeps.

clue.text: Agree the artist is a monster!

parts.note: to chime in agreement, to chime with
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that the painter is a beast!
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: A baker's turnover?

parts.note: a turnover is a pastry, but here it is something a baker ... over, a bread item

explanation.definitionFit: A bread roll is a baker's product, and to roll is to turn over.

clue.text: The issue drink eventually becomes

parts.note: an issue is an outcome, an end
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone notices what a drink finally turns into.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up as something is to finish by becoming it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: The most intimate occur within the home

indicators.note: within means the occurring word sits inside the home

parts.note: a nest is a home
things that are exist, they occur

explanation.surface: Those closest to us gather at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occur' gives ARE in its sense of exist; 'The' belongs to the definition, the most intimate ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Your closest friends are those nearest and dearest, the most familiar.

clue.text: Withdraw public transport set-up the area under-used

indicators.note: under signals that the first piece sits under the area in the down entry
in a down clue, set up means the word is turned and read upwards

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Withdraw the bus service built in a district where few use it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' reverses BUS to SUB, and 'under' places it above TRACT in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away, deduct, as a sum is taken out.

clue.text: Cross through the work of a rhymster

parts.note: per means through or by means of
a rhymster writes verse

explanation.surface: Annoyed by a poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A perverse person is contrary and awkward, much like a cross, ill-tempered one.

clue.text: There isn't very much so parcel it out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are spread out and laid again in a different order

explanation.surface: Since there is hardly anything there, divide the parcel up and share it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on PARCEL IT; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute amount, a tiny bit of something.

clue.text: A slight bend in the road

definitions.text: A slight bend in the road

parts.words: A slight bend in the road
parts.note: reads like a gentle curve on a route, but means the slight upward curve across a road's surface for drainage

explanation.definitionFit: Roads are built with a convex cross-section so rain runs off to the sides; that curvature has its own name.

clue.text: Distance from main road to field and back for example

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: back means the example abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia

explanation.surface: How far it is from the main road to the field and back, say.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as I. 'back' turns EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileage is a distance counted in miles.

clue.text: Cavalryman capturing a forager

indicators.note: capturing means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a cavalryman is a horseman, a rider

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier seizes someone foraging for supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider goes out plundering or foraging for food and loot in enemy territory.

clue.text: Having to remain around, measure natural growth

indicators.note: around means the first piece's letters are wrapped round the measure

parts.note: to lie is to remain in a state, as land lies fallow
a metre is a unit of measure

explanation.surface: A rule about measuring how much things grow when left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE means remain, as land lies fallow; 'Having' is a link. The hyphenated answer is the linden, not the citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime tree (linden) is an example of something that grows naturally, a plant.

clue.text: Article on an idle rebellious girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the article sits on top of what follows

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rebellious suggests letters refusing their order and rising up out of place

parts.note: the printed AN IDLE stands for E, N, I, D, L, E: the setter's fodder slipped an A for an E

explanation.surface: A piece on a lazy, defiant young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, A + an anagram of AN IDLE gives two As; the name needs an E, so the setter's fodder seems slipped by a letter. 'rebellious' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adeline is a woman's given name.

clue.text: They'll offer light support, though quite powerless

definitions.text: They'll offer light support, though quite powerless

parts.words: They'll offer light support, though quite powerless
parts.note: items that hold up a source of light yet need no electrical power at all

explanation.definitionFit: Candle holders literally support a light, and a candle burns without mains electricity.

clue.text: Produce notes about a bird that's fast-moving

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes round the bird

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
the coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A bird that sings and moves quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce notes' looks like making a memo but means to sing; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooting is going along rapidly, dashing off.

clue.text: Not in the majority as yet

definitions.text: Not in the majority as yet

parts.words: Not in the majority as yet
parts.note: majority read as the age of legal adulthood, not the larger group

explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet of legal adult age is a minor, still too young.

clue.text: An expert in his own field choosing colt for breaking

definitions.text: An expert in his own field

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and reassembled, as a horse is broken in

explanation.surface: A horse specialist picks out a young colt to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for breaking' suggests breaking in a colt, but it is the anagram signal on CHOOSING COLT.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who studies shells (molluscs) is a scientist expert in that particular field of zoology.

clue.text: Mistreatment of the soil should be opposed

indicators.note: mistreatment suggests the letters are knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Abuse of farmland ought to be resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistreatment of' is the anagram signal on THE SOIL; 'should be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means antagonistic, set against.

clue.text: Decide about a place in Washington

indicators.note: about means the deciding word goes round the article

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Choose somewhere to live in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the US state, not the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State.

clue.text: A carriage of bygone days — sound, well-constructed

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is said aloud, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: handsome in the sense of well-proportioned, finely made

explanation.surface: An old-time carriage, solid and well built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like it means sturdy, alongside well-constructed, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hansom cab was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of Victorian times.

clue.text: The man left in bed to be observed

indicators.note: in means the man and the left sign go inside the bed

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man left lying in bed to be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; 'The man' is the usual crossword source of HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past participle of behold, to see.

clue.text: Honour a worker without one's showing respect

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the honour-and-worker pair sits around the next piece

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
one's is I (one) plus S, i.e. 'one is' shortened

explanation.surface: Decorating an employee without fanfare as a sign of esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and one's is read as I's (one is).
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant describes someone bowing or deferring, showing deference.

clue.text: Pressed to include a married lady

indicators.note: to include means the first word holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: pressed in the sense of forced or made to do something

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to count a wedded woman among the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts A and M inside MADE, giving MAD-AM-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a woman, a title like Mrs.

clue.text: Take the plunge and get into the swim

definitions.meaning: to throw oneself into an activity, plunge in

explanation.definitionFit: To dive is literally to plunge into water and figuratively to launch eagerly into something.

clue.text: Characters having a certain leaning may well indicate stress

definitions.meaning: a typeface used to show emphasis

explanation.definitionFit: Slanted type letters lean to the right and are the usual print device for emphasis.

clue.text: Awfully staid set giving rise to some antipathy

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated and left in disorder

explanation.surface: A sedate crowd provokes dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' is the anagram signal on STAID SET; 'giving rise to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, close to antipathy.

clue.text: Making the old king look right — older looking

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Doing up an ageing monarch so he looks proper.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the cipher of King George seen on British pillar boxes; 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair going more grey makes a person look aged.

clue.text: Army personnel counted as discharged

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to be deemed is to be considered or counted as

explanation.surface: Soldiers deemed fit for release from service.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise or debt that is redeemed has been fulfilled, discharged.
